author: hangleang
content: I have a few questions on builder blacklisting design while implementing along side the circuit breaker. (1) should blacklisted builders' bid be propagated or forwarded to our peers? (2) what payload status should be consider its builder to be blacklisted? is the decision based on local view or PTC votes?

author: nflaig
content: gonna answer this so that potuz can correct my wrong response later, so for (1) I think we should not apply this to p2p bids at all, only for direct builders, and (2) if the block was strong and payload was not revealed it should be counted as a fault

author: hangleang
content: Agree for (1) we should accept and forward, but also filter out their bids from value comparison (highest bid), otherwise they can suppress honest builders from acceptance

author: potuz
content: Terence also agrees with you but I implemented dropping bids from blacklisted builders and not propagating them. The rationale was that if we blacklist a builder is because we think it's a danger for the chain and therefore we shouldn't propagate that bid. I'm willing to change that view though. Cc <@363800010518822915> I should have taken your bet: it wasn't AI that found about this 🙂

author: nflaig
content:
> therefore we shouldn't propagate that bid
shouldn't the circuit breaker stay local only and not affect p2p propagation, or otherwise should this be part of the spec? anyways I feel like this is pointless, p2p bids can be sybil attacked easily, so using builder pubkey/index to blacklist doesn't make sense. I am mean sure you can do that but I wouldn't add this if it adds extra complexity

author: terencechain
content: That’s my pt. Any subjective client decision to IGNORE should be well documented, whether in the p2p spec or a client specific spec. Whether clients should ignore it is a separate debate that I care less about. In general, I’m against spending too much time debating p2p behavior for a scenario where, in practice, only around 0.1% of bids will win. The main thing I care about is making sure a node can’t be dos'ed by bids

author: tersec
content: yeah agree with this, if the circuit breaker conditions affect gossip, then the circuit breaker details are consensus

author: tersec
content: thus I prefer it not affect gossip

author: potuz
content: I would argue that the circuit breaker is akin to a DOS protection: we are preventing these bids from propagating cause we think these bids are eclipsing other valid bids that will deliver a payload

author: potuz
content:
Anyway, I think that my order of preference would be 
1. Clients do whatever they want,  Prysm Drops, not put anything in consensus. 
2. if people dislike the above I'm willing to make Prysm not drop. 

But what I definitely don't want to do under any circumstances is adding circuit breaker details to consensus. Lets stop wasting time specifying this stupid gossip path

author: terencechain
content: it's not documenting to consensus. It's documenting your behavior somewhere such that the next person can refer to and no history gets lost. Today's discord conversation will surely get lost and years after years ppl are going to come back with the same question why is prysm behaving like this. I dont care if its in the p2p spec or your personal blog but you should be somewhere that can be referenced to down the line

author: potuz
content: happy to add to my blog 😉

content: if clients are independently making decisions to drop bids in a way that is not in the specs - doesn't this allow clients to arbitrarily censor bids?
